version.changelog:
- Updated SKILL.md to clarify APIDot GPT Image 2 API entry points and usage flows.
- Added a "Start on APIDot" section with direct links for onboarding from ClawHub.
- No longer ships skill-card.md; now only SKILL.md and non-executable notes remain.
- No changes to main guidance, workflows, or API field coverage.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only APIDot GPT Image 2 helper with disclosed API-key handling guidance and no executable behavior.

dimensions.detail: It names an optional APIDOT_API_KEY and discusses private prompts, image URLs, callbacks, and task IDs, but only as integration guidance and with clear warnings to keep secrets server-side and out of logs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown files only, no executable files, install-time automation, bundled clients, or dependency installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to documentation lookup, request planning, credential hygiene, polling, and webhook guidance, with explicit direction not to make live API calls unless the user asks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, or tool modification is present; persistence guidance is limited to application-level storage of task metadata for async image jobs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to route GPT Image 2 APIDot integration work to docs, examples, and async workflow notes; the artifact contents match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers should treat this as a reference skill, not a client library. Use a server-side APIDot key only when intentionally making APIDot calls, and avoid exposing prompts, private image URLs, callback URLs, generated URLs, or API keys in frontend code or logs.
